findings.title: Do not grant group management from the view scope
findings.body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses this check to authorize both creating groups and moving existing subgroups to the top level. Consequently, an administrator granted only read-only access to all groups can perform these mutations. Require MANAGE here and add a negative test that attempts these operations with only VIEW.

findings.title: Return group model IDs rather than authorization resource IDs
findings.body: groupResource.getId() is the authorization resource's generated ID, not the GroupModel ID (which the schema stores as the resource name). Passing it to hasPermission() therefore misses the resource lookup by name, and adding it to the returned set supplies invalid group IDs to user search/count filtering. In particular, granting VIEW_MEMBERS on all groups causes the synthetic Groups resource's ID to be returned, so user searches are restricted to a nonexistent group and return no members. Evaluate actual group IDs, and handle the all-groups resource separately rather than returning its authorization ID.

findings.title: Enable group-member creation for V2 permissions
findings.body: The fallback for creating users in managed groups still requires the V1 ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature. With only V2 enabled, an administrator granted the new MANAGE_MEMBERS and MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP scopes on a group is rejected before either group permission is evaluated when POSTing a user assigned to that group. Extend this feature gate to V2 and test creation using group-scoped permissions without global user-management permission.
